title: The Bog Bodies
text: Bodies in the peat, perfectly kept, faces calm, skin brown and smooth as tanned leather. Some still wear gold at their throats and rings on their fingers. The marsh folk say they were offerings, given to the bog so it would give something back.

options.label: Take the gold from their throats. The bog has kept it long enough.

outcomes.text: The old gold is cold and heavy. The calm faces do not change, at least not that you can see.
The bodies sit up, peat sliding from their faces, and reach for what was theirs.

options.label: The wisest studies the marks cut into them, hoping to learn what was paid for.

outcomes.text: The marks are those of the old marsh gods: their names, cut into the skin beside what each body was given for. Some of those gifts are still owed.

options.label: Push them gently back under, and leave the offerings to the bog.

outcomes.text: The peat closes over their calm faces. The marsh seems grateful, opening a dry path ahead.
